name: ROSTA Window stencil poster
summary: A strip of cartoon panels with short rhymed captions, cut as paper stencils and painted by hand, then copied for shop windows. The flat colour, thick black contour and fast brush work follow from the speed of the news.

philosophy.core_thesis: A news poster that artists can paint in one night must use few flat colours, a heavy contour and a rhyme that a passer-by reads in seconds.
design_principles: Split each message into 4–12 panels in one strip; give each panel one figure and one short line of verse.
Draw a heavy black contour of 3–6 mm round each figure; it holds the shape when a stencil shifts.
Use 3–5 flat opaque colours: red, yellow ochre, blue and black. Do not blend them.
Cut one paper stencil for each colour and keep the bridges that hold the islands in place.
Letter the caption by hand, in capitals, in the same black as the contour.
Make the enemy small, ugly and clear; make the worker large, in red.
Paint on cheap wrapping paper or newsprint, and leave the brush edges and drips.
anti_patterns: A smooth gradient or a soft shadow
Small text that a passer-by cannot read at 5 m

process.matrix: Paper or card stencils, one for each colour, cut by hand from a drawn master.
process.press: None. A brush or a spray puts the paint through each stencil by hand.
process.image_making: An artist draws the master strip. A team cuts the stencils and paints the sheets panel by panel.
process.edition: Dozens to a few hundred sheets for each window; no two painted sheets match.

inks.strategy: Opaque poster paint through stencils, one flat colour at a time, with the black contour last.

colours.name: Red
colours.role: the flag, the worker and the accent

screening.rule: Make no tone. Fill each area with one flat colour, and use the bare paper for light.

registration.rule: A stencil shifts 1–3 mm on the sheet. The heavy contour hides the gap, and the bare paper shows at some edges.

substrate.stock: Cheap wrapping paper or newsprint, grey-brown, glued in strips if the window is wide.
substrate.finish: Uncoated, with a rough tooth that takes thick paint.

surface.impression: No bite; the paint dries on the surface of the sheet.
surface.sheen: Matt, with a slight gloss where the paint is thick.
surface.texture: Brush marks, paint drips, stencil bridges and a cockle in the thin sheet.

marks: colour that stops short of the contour

emotion.target_response: Quick, loud wit: the viewer reads a street cartoon with a verse, painted by hand that week, and feels that the news is urgent.

avoid_when: The message needs a photograph or fine detail.
The tone must be calm, neutral or premium.

modifiers.how: Keep the red and black blocks and the heavy lettering; add cut-out halftone photographs on a diagonal layout.
Keep the coarse outline and flat colour; drop the strip layout and put the hand colour loosely over a black key line.

screen_ruling.note: The style makes no tone; the screen stays at zero.
